---

On the Development Seed blog, [Brianna Corremonte][Brianna] has published [a 
thought-provoking article on social debt][article] and how it is exacerbated in 
the age of AI and agentic coding[^agentic-coding]. Social debt is the 
"cumulative and increasing cost (...) connected to invisible and negative 
effects within a development community." 

Brianna mentions recent discussions on AI around [terrio][terrio] (a Rust 
library for geospatial data transformation created using agentic coding) and 
[around AI contributions in the GDAL community][disc][^gdal]. This reminded me 
of [the talk by Anita Graser][talk] (pdf) at the [2026 QGIS User 
Conference][qgis] in which she detailled implications of agentic coding for the 
open-source community and how various open-source projects deal with them.

In her [article][article], Brianna argues that "[t]he already fragile social 
infrastructure of open source communities is now at real risk of breaking under 
AI" and that under-represented people may feel the fallout most. She lists 
a few examples of AI accelerating social debt:

> Newcomers are disappearing and AI is replacing the old process of asking in 
public and someone inviting a new person in. (...) 
> 
> Maintainers are also being overwhelmed by AI-generated PRs[^prs], adding to 
more burnout. (...)
>
> Lone wolf is becoming the default mode which will result in more silos, 
fragmentation and an excessive volume of new tools. When you can get an answer, 
generate code and ship a tool without ever talking to another person, working 
alone becomes the path of least resistance.

Brianna concludes:

> (...) what we need are more tangible ways to pay down our social debt, treated 
with the same urgency and planning we give technical debt. What if, for every 
technical backlog refinement meeting, we set aside the same time for reducing 
social debt?

The article gives some positive examples of how communities can heed this call 
to action. [Food for thought][article]!

[terrio]: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/my-response-criticisms-recent-open-source-projects-qiusheng-wu-6tyie
[disc]: https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/pull/15399#issuecomment-6212682661
[talk]: https://talks.osgeo.org/media/qgis-uc2026/submissions/YKQSPT/resources/QGIS.ORG_-_QUC2026_Laax_-_AI_in_the_PnhvcEj.pdf
[qgis]: https://conference.qgis.org/

[^agentic-coding]: Software development in which AI agents autonomously plan, 
write, run, and revise code across multiple steps, with the human mainly setting 
goals and reviewing results.
[^gdal]: [GDAL](https://gdal.org/) (Geospatial Data Abstraction Library) is an 
open-source library and set of command-line tools for reading, writing, and 
transforming raster and vector geospatial data formats.
[^prs]: Pull requests, that is, proposed code changes submitted to a project for 
review and merging.
